body.p: In this amendment, claims 1-18 and 21-22 are pending, with claims 1, 10, and 21 being independent. Claims 1-5, 7, 9-14, and 16-18 are amended. Claims 19 and 20 are canceled. Claims 21 and 22 have been added. As the number of independent claims and the total number of claims now pending does not exceed that which were originally paid for upon filing, no fee is believed due in consequence of the added claims. Support for these amendments can be found at least in paragraphs 41-43, 55, 64, 67-68, 78-79, and 93, and in FIGS. 2A and 2B of Applicant's disclosure. No new matter has been added.

Applicant acknowledges, with appreciation, Examiners Park and Henson for participating in the telephonic interview (Interview) conducted on March 15, 2024, with the undersigned. During the Interview, no exhibit was shown, and no demonstration was conducted. Potential amendments to claim 1 were discussed in connection with the rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 102. The Examiners indicated that while the proposed amendments appear to overcome the current reference, further consideration of the proposed amendments and further searching would be required.
35 U.S.C. @ 102 Rejections: Claims 1-20
Claims 1-20 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(2) as being allegedly anticipated by U.S. Publication No. 20210150873 to Shouldice et al. (Shouldice).
Amended claim 1 recites:
A method of monitoring a user's breathing, the method comprising:
passively monitoring the user's breathing with a device during a
predetermined time interval generating sensor-generated signals, wherein the sensor-generated signals include acoustic signals comprising audio and motion
signals;
identifying a breathing mode of the user's breathing and detecting that the

breathing mode is a particular trigger mode selected from a plurality of detectable trigger modes including shallow breathing and mouth breathing by processing data created from the sensor-generated signals using a machine learning model trained, at least in part, to distinguish between shallow breathing and mouth breathing; and
responsive to detecting the trigger mode, providing to the user via the device
real time biofeedback specifying a breathing exercise adapted to the particular
trigger mode.

As amended, claim 1 clarifies that the sensor-generated signals include "acoustic signals comprising audio and motion signals." Further, the trigger modes that are detectable include "shallow breathing and mouth breathing." As such, the machine learning model is "trained, at least in part, to distinguish between shallow breathing and mouth breathing."

Applicant respectfully submits that Shouldice does not disclose or suggest the ability to detect mouth breathing let alone the ability to distinguish between shallow breathing and mouth breathing by way of a machine learning model. In addition, to the extent that the biofeedback is adapted to the trigger mode, Shouldice is unable to provide biofeedback adapted to mouth breathing.
Applicant's remarks supporting patentability of claim 1 are relevant to claim 10 and are hereby reiterated in support thereof.
As amended, claim 2 recites, in part:
detecting a plurality of phases of the user's breathing by processing the
audio of the acoustic signals using an additional machine learning model;
wherein the additional machine learning model is trained as a student model

in a teacher-student architecture including a teacher model, wherein the teacher model is configured to generate labels for received motion training data, wherein the additional machine learning model uses the labels in learning to classify training audio into the plurality of breathing phases, and wherein the training audio is time
aligned with the motion training data.

As amended, claim 2 clarifies that the identifying breathing modes includes detecting breathing phases (e.g., inhalation and exhalation) using an additional machine learning model. The manner in which the additional machine learning model is trained uses a teacher-student architecture in which a teacher model generates labels for received motion data and the labels, as generated, are used to train the additional machine learning model (the student model) to correctly classify audio data.
Amended claim 2 further clarifies that data of a first modality, e.g., motion data, is used to generate labels used to train a machine learning model to correctly classify data of a second and
different modality (e.g., audio/acoustic signals). Shouldice does not disclose or suggest such features.
Applicant's remarks supporting patentability of claim 2 are relevant to claim 11 and are hereby reiterated in support thereof.
As amended, claim 5 recites, in part:
identifying a social context corresponding to the user in which the user is
engaged in a conversation based on detection of human voices; and
in response to the identifying the social context, delaying the providing of
the biofeedback to the user.

As amended, claim 5 recites operations in which the biofeedback is delayed in response to identifying the user is in the social context of being engaged in a conversation. The biofeedback is delayed so as to avoid providing notifications at times likely considered to be a nuisance to the user or others around the user.
Applicant's remarks supporting patentability of claim 5 are relevant to claim 14 and are hereby reiterated in support thereof.
The remaining claims are believed to patentably define over Shouldice in view of their own merits and their dependence on the underlying claims.
In view of the foregoing, withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(2) rejection of claims 1-20 is respectfully requested.

New claims 19 and 20 are believed to recite features not disclosed or suggested by Shouldice. Claim 19, for example, is directed to monitoring a user's breathing by detecting breathing phases using a machine learning model trained using a teacher-student architecture. Claim 20 detects whether a breathing mode is a trigger mode.

Reconsideration and a Notice of Allowance are respectfully requested in view of the amended claims and the Remarks presented above. If there are any questions, a telephone call to the undersigned is invited.
Respectfully submitted,
